correctness.rationale: The unique deep peak follows from the explicit two-exponential impulse kernel, whose derivative after pulse shutdown changes sign exactly once. The interval-mean representation of delay is strictly decreasing in each eigenvalue; variational derivatives for the symmetric generalized eigenproblem give rigorous strict eigenvalue signs for all four positive physical parameters. The duration derivative is strictly in (0,1) via elementary exponential inequalities. Boundaries and zero initial conditions are explicit. The attached program verifies polynomial identities exactly and representative numeric points but is not used to infer universal validity.

originality.rationale: The original two-box transfer solution and superposition are explicitly acknowledged as previously published. The newly isolated claim is an all-positive-parameter theorem: one post-pulse deep peak with an exact time and strict monotonicity in every one of the four independent physical parameters and forcing duration. Substantive inspected material from the motivating 2013 study, full earlier 2010 author-hosted PDF, and later 2019 free HTML did not state this conjunction or a statement implying the sign of every parameter derivative. Database searches found no dominating equivalent, though they are not novelty proofs. An inaccessible appendix/general thermal-network statement is a documented residual risk.

No claim of absolute database uniqueness or independent audit; searches are not mathematical proof of originality.

value.rationale: A stopped forcing experiment presents a physically meaningful question: how late can the deep thermal reservoir reach its maximum after a surface input ends? The theorem replaces a qualitative two-timescale narrative with a unique exact peak and globally fixed signs under every heat capacity, feedback and exchange perturbation. This can guide the relative timing of follow-up measurements and sensitivity analysis without parameter calibration. Its contribution is the nontrivial strict ordering for all positive coefficients, not the routine superposition of existing step solutions.
